assessments.sourceExcerpt: My team and I built a digital and assisted digital service (no paper version) to meet a need that hadn’t previously existed. We passed alpha and beta Service Standard assessments and launched to the public in only 12 weeks.
assessments.sourceMeaning: The author and their team built the POA-refund service and launched it publicly; the surrounding source identifies the author as its Product Manager.
assessments.explanation: The source attributes building the service to the author and team and reports its public launch.

assessments.sourceExcerpt: launched to the public in only 12 weeks.
assessments.sourceMeaning: The service was publicly launched in a twelve-week delivery period.
assessments.explanation: “Na twaalf weken” conveys the reported twelve-week period; the source does not specify a more precise starting point.

assessments.sourceExcerpt: We were initially asked to deliver the service in a matter of weeks
assessments.sourceMeaning: The initial request was to deliver the service within a short period measured in weeks.
assessments.explanation: “Enkele weken” is a reasonable rendering of “a matter of weeks.”

assessments.sourceExcerpt: we quickly discovered would not be possible if we wanted to create a quality service for our users.
assessments.sourceMeaning: The team judged delivery within the initially requested period infeasible if it was to create a quality service for users.
assessments.explanation: The narrative preserves both the team's judgment and the condition of maintaining service quality.

assessments.sourceExcerpt: My team focused on the users applying for refunds first
assessments.sourceMeaning: The team focused first on users applying for refunds.
assessments.explanation: Working out the applicant experience first accurately conveys this priority.

assessments.sourceExcerpt: Plans for the caseworker user came later.
assessments.sourceMeaning: Caseworker plans came after the initial focus on refund applicants.
assessments.explanation: The narrative preserves the stated order.

assessments.sourceExcerpt: We achieved this by splitting our fortnightly sprints in two: testing, researching and accepting applications in the first week and then suspending submissions to concentrate on testing, researching and processing applications the second.
assessments.sourceMeaning: During private beta, the team divided each two-week sprint into scheduled periods that included research and testing.
assessments.explanation: The recurring split of the sprints supports the description of time set aside for research and testing.
